problem: The lead says "Every gate on several qubits is then a matrix formed by the Kronecker product". That is false: a Kronecker product A ⊗ B only builds gates that act on the qubits one at a time. CNOT and other genuinely joint multi-qubit gates are not Kronecker products, and Section 3 of this same chapter says so, so the lead contradicts the body and will mislead a student.
fix: Say: "A gate that acts on one qubit at a time is a matrix formed by the Kronecker product; a gate that acts on several qubits jointly, such as CNOT, is a general 4×4 unitary that need not be any single Kronecker product."

problem: "the product space has mn dimensions" reads as if the space has mn different dimensions; the standard wording is that its dimension is mn.
fix: "so the product space has dimension mn (a single number)."

problem: "A sum m + n would describe a state that lies in one space or the other, not in both at once" is loose: the direct sum V ⊕ W does have dimension m + n and holds a pair of vectors. What it fails to give is the product amplitudes cij = vi wj, the cross terms between the two systems.
fix: "A basis of V ⊗ W is every pair |i⟩ ⊗ |j⟩, giving m × n vectors. The direct sum V ⊕ W has only m + n basis vectors, because it keeps the two lists separate and never forms pairs; it cannot carry the products vi wj that a joint amplitude needs."

problem: "compress the mn-sized vectors of many-body systems" uses mn, the two-factor symbol from earlier. For n qubits the joint vector has 2ⁿ amplitudes, not mn, so the size is understated and the notation is confusing here.
fix: "compress the exponentially large joint vectors of many-body systems (2ⁿ amplitudes for n qubits)".
